title: One-Skillet Creamy Lemon Chicken Gnocchi
imagePrompt: Plump potato gnocchi and shreds of rotisserie chicken sit in a glossy, ivory cream sauce flecked with cracked black pepper and pale green thyme. Wilted baby spinach leaves are folded throughout, their deep green threading through the pale sauce, and a light dusting of melted parmesan clings to the ridges of the gnocchi. Bright flecks of lemon zest catch the light across the top, with a few red-pepper flakes adding small bursts of orange.
subtitle: A 20-minute one-skillet dinner: gnocchi simmered right in a lemon cream sauce with rotisserie chicken, spinach, and parmesan.

ingredients.heading: Ingredients
ingredients.note: The quick version of our rotisserie chicken gnocchi bake -- same cozy flavors, no oven, no bacon, no mushrooms, done in one skillet.
ingredients.callout: Important: Add the lemon juice only after the heat is off -- stirring it into a hot cream sauce can cause the cream to break.

body.html: The fast, weeknight version: raw gnocchi simmers directly in a broth-and-cream sauce, rotisserie chicken and spinach fold in at the end, and parmesan plus a hit of lemon finish it off the heat. One skillet, no oven, about 20 minutes start to finish.

items: Simmer gnocchi in broth and cream until tender
Fold in chicken and spinach to warm through and wilt
Off heat, stir in parmesan, lemon zest, and lemon juice

body.html: Key rule: Add the lemon juice after you turn off the heat -- that's what keeps the cream sauce smooth instead of curdled.

slides.title: Melt Butter + Bloom Garlic
slides.checkboxLabel: Butter melted, garlic and thyme bloomed

items: Melt the butter in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add the garlic, thyme (or Italian seasoning), and optional red-pepper flakes.
Cook about 30 seconds, just until fragrant -- don't let the garlic brown.

body.html: Shortcut: Jarred minced garlic works fine here and saves the mincing step entirely.

items: Add the chicken broth, heavy cream, gnocchi, 1/4 tsp salt, and plenty of black pepper. Stir and bring to a gentle simmer.
Cover and cook 4-6 minutes, stirring once or twice, until the gnocchi is tender.
Keep the heat moderate so the cream doesn't scorch.

body.html: Why the broth matters: It's what actually cooks the gnocchi -- there's no separate pot of boiling water in this version.

items: Cook uncovered for 2-3 minutes, until the chicken is hot and the spinach has wilted.

body.html: Rotisserie rule: The chicken is already cooked, so you're just warming it through -- don't let it simmer long enough to dry out.

slides.title: Finish with Parmesan + Lemon
slides.checkboxLabel: Off heat: parmesan, lemon zest, and juice stirred in

items: Turn off the heat. Stir in the parmesan, the zest of half the lemon, and 1 tbsp lemon juice.
Taste and add more salt, pepper, or lemon if needed.
Let it stand 2 minutes before serving.

body.html: Adjust the texture: If the sauce is too thick, loosen it with a splash of broth. If it's thin, stir in a little more parmesan and let it sit a minute.
